  of product cards with images, names, and prices

  pages

input.prompt:
Build a full multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.", a handmade crafts shop. Full details below.

PROJECT DETAILS:
- Business: Artisan Goods Co. — handmade crafts shop
- Categories: Pottery, Textiles, Woodwork, Jewelry
- Audience: Craft lovers, gift shoppers, design-conscious consumers
- Goal: Showcase products, tell the brand story, capture newsletter leads

DESIGN DIRECTION:
Warm, artisanal aesthetic that feels handcrafted and authentic — like a well-curated boutique market stall brought online. Rich earth tones, natural textures, and generous whitespace. NOT a generic e-commerce template — this should feel personal and crafted.

LAYOUT TYPE: Standard
Multi-page marketing/shop site with full navigation header and footer.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
- Color: Warm earth palette — terracotta, warm cream/off-white, deep walnut brown, sage green accent. Nothing cold or corporate.
- Typography: Serif display font for headings (warmth, craft heritage feel), clean sans-serif for body. Generous line-height.
- Layout: Asymmetric hero with full-bleed imagery. Product grid with subtle hover lifts. NO uniform icon grids.

VISUAL ELEMENTS:
- Primary: Photography — search for artisan/handmade craft product photos (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry)
- Style: Warm natural lighting, tactile textures, close-up detail shots
- Application: Full-bleed hero, product cards, team profile photos on About page
- Logo: Generate a logo using the media-logo skill — wordmark style with a small hand-drawn craft icon (e.g. a simple pottery wheel or leaf motif), warm terracotta/brown color

MOTION DESIGN:
- Level: Subtle
- Effects: Fade-in on scroll for sections (350ms ease-out), hover lift on product cards (translate-y -4px + shadow), smooth nav link underline draw on hover
- Personality: Warm and unhurried — nothing snappy or corporate

SECTION-SPECIFIC:

Hero (Homepage):
- Full-bleed background image of artisan at work or product flatlay
- Headline: "Handcrafted with Heart" — large serif, overlaid on image with warm overlay
- Subheadline and CTA button ("Shop the Collection" → /products)
- Subtle fade-in entrance animation

Featured Products (Homepage):
- Section title "Our Favorites" in serif
- 4 featured product cards in a 2x2 or horizontal scroll on mobile
- Each card: product image, name, category tag, price
- Hover: lift effect + subtle shadow

Newsletter Signup (Homepage):
- Warm-toned band section (terracotta or deep brown background)
- Headline: "Join Our Community"
- Email input + Subscribe button
- NOT a centered-on-band generic CTA — use asymmetric layout with decorative element

Product Catalog Page (/products):
- Page title + breadcrumb
- Category filter tabs: All | Pottery | Textiles | Woodwork | Jewelry
- Products fetched from /api/products (with optional ?category= query param)
- Responsive grid: 3 cols desktop, 2 cols tablet, 1 col mobile
- Product card: image, name, category badge, price
- Loading skeleton state while fetching
- Filter updates the displayed products (client-side filter or re-fetch)

About Page (/about):
- Hero section: "Our Story" with a warm full-bleed image
- Brand story paragraph (2-3 paragraphs about handmade craft values)
- Mission statement in a pull-quote style (large serif, centered, terracotta accent)
- Team section: 3 team member cards with photo, name, role, short bio
- Staggered fade-in on scroll for team cards

Shared Header:
- Logo left, nav links right: Home | Shop | About
- Active link indicator (underline or color)
- Mobile hamburger menu with slide-in drawer
- Warm cream/off-white background, walnut brown text

Shared Footer:
- 3-column: Brand blurb + logo | Quick links | Newsletter mini-signup or social links
- Warm dark background (deep walnut/charcoal), cream text
- Maintain design quality — not an afterthought

DIFFERENTIATION:
Asymmetric hero with large serif headline breaking the grid. Product cards use a warm paper-texture-inspired card background. Pull-quote mission statement on About page creates a memorable typographic moment.

CONSISTENCY:
Maintain warm earth-tone energy throughout all pages and the footer. Animation timing consistent (subtle, 300-400ms). Serif/sans pairing used consistently across all pages.

BUILD ORDER:

Phase 1 — Setup (run in parallel):
- Search for images: hero (artisan at work / craft flatlay), product images for each category (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry), team member photos, about page hero
- Generate logo using media-logo skill (wordmark + craft icon, terracotta/brown)
- Set font stack using fontTheme tool — serif display (e.g. Playfair Display or Lora) + clean sans (e.g. DM Sans or Nunito)
- Set color scheme using colorScheme tool — terracotta primary, warm cream background, walnut brown foreground, sage green accent

Phase 2 — API + Routes (after Phase 1):
- Create src/server/api/products.ts — Express handler for GET /api/products with optional ?category= filter. Returns array of 12–16 mock products across all 4 categories with id, name, category, price, image fields. Import and register in src/server/entry.ts.
- Add routes to src/routes.tsx: / (homepage), /products (catalog), /about

Phase 3 — Layout (after Phase 1):
- Update src/layouts/parts/Header.tsx — warm cream bg, logo, nav links (Home/Shop/About), active state, mobile drawer
- Update src/layouts/parts/Footer.tsx — 3-column dark footer with brand blurb, quick links, social icons

Phase 4 — Pages (after Phase 2 & 3):
- Build src/pages/index.tsx — homepage with hero, featured products (fetch from /api/products, show first 4), newsletter signup
- Build src/pages/products.tsx — catalog page with category filter tabs, full product grid fetched from /api/products, loading skeletons
- Build src/pages/about.tsx — story, mission pull-quote, team profiles

Phase 5 — Finalize:
- Mark all todo items as COMPLETE using the todoList tool
- Show the design and ask for feedback using askQuestion

CRITICAL: Build pages LAST — after setup, API, header, and footer are complete.

TODO LIST IDs (mark complete when done):

- Product catalog page: 1780065617358-bhrx09x
- About page: 1780065617358-b2xjj6w
- Shared navigation & footer: 1780065617358-hc96kia
- Products API endpoint: 1780065617358-dlxtmi6
List ID: 1780065617357-o7m011w

INITIAL SCOPE: Build all pages as specified — this is a full multi-page site request.

DESIGN FEEDBACK:
After showing the site, use askQuestion to ask:
- "What do you think of the design?"
- Suggestions: ["Looks great!", "Adjust the color scheme", "Change the fonts", "Tweak the product layout", "Add a product detail page"]

turns.content: I want to make sure every page — homepage, products, and about — all share the same header and footer automatically, without each page having to add those components individually. Is that handled through a shared layout component that wraps all routes, or does each page manually include the header and footer?

The shared layout is already handled automatically — you don't need to touch it. Here's how it works:

**`src/App.tsx`** wraps all routes in a single `RootLayout` via React Router's `<Outlet>` pattern:

```tsx
const rootElement = (
  <RootLayout>
    <Outlet />   // ← every page renders here
  </RootLayout>
);

const routeTree = [{ element: rootElement, children: routes }];
```

**`src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx`** renders the header and footer once, around whatever page is active:

```tsx
<Website>
  <Header />
  {children}   // ← the current page's content
  <Footer />
</Website>
```

So when you add a new route to `src/routes.tsx`, it automatically gets the header and footer — no imports needed in the page file itself. The pages (`index.tsx`, `products.tsx`, `about.tsx`) only contain their own content, nothing else.

If you ever want a page *without* the shared chrome (a full-screen game, a standalone landing page, etc.), you'd add it as a separate route tree outside that wrapper in `App.tsx` — but for standard pages, it's fully automatic.

This is exactly what I needed to hear. The site is looking really solid. I think we're in good shape — thanks for building this out so thoroughly!
